brief: US October core CPI rose 0.3% MoM SA for a third straight month. Unlike August and September, which were driven by volatile items (airfares, hotels, telephone services) and the super-weak -0.02% June print, October's strength was broad: OER, car insurance and recreation services were all firm, and core goods excluding the volatile airfare downside surprise were stronger than expected. The 1Y TIPS breakeven widened about 10bp on the release. CA-CIB reads this solid CPI plus last Friday's hot jobs report as essentially locking in a Fed hike at the December meeting, maintaining its base case of a 25bp hike. Separately, preliminary Eurozone core HICP for October printed 2.54% YoY, 8bp above CA-CIB's 2.46% preview, with some but not all of the upside from noisy components (hotels, clothing). Despite recently easing energy prices, CA-CIB expects further Eurozone core inflation acceleration to 2.6% at year-end and 2.8-2.9% in early 2027, as higher gas and oil prices and a weaker EUR/USD argue for upward ECB forecast revisions, with tighter financial conditions the only significant mitigant. CA-CIB's own 2027 core average forecast of 2.9% sits 30bp above the ECB's September projection.
